english.title: Breach a forced marriage protection order

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: antisocial behaviour crime and policing act 2014

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, breached a forced marriage protection order imposed by **(..SPECIFY THE COURT..) on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE ON WHICH THE ORDER WAS IMPOSED..) under section

(A)_[63A(1)]_
(B)_[63D(1)]_

of the Family Law Act 1996 by doing an act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), which was prohibited by that Order
english.legislation: Contrary to section 63CA(1) and (5) of the Family Law Act 1996.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
without reasonable excuse
acted in a way prohibited by a forced marriage protection order

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) In the case of a forced marriage protection order made by virtue of section 63D(1), a person can be guilty of an offence under this section only in respect of conduct engaged in at a time when the person was aware of the existence of the order.
(ii) Where a person is convicted of an offence under this section in respect of any conduct, that conduct is not punishable as a contempt of court.
(iii) This offence applies only in relation to conduct occurring on or after the day on which it comes into force (16th June 2014).

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note: In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to 12 months imprisonment is to be read as a reference to six months.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None
